blocking.claim: docs/22 line 114: 'That is the shipped rule, and the probe's last line confirms the module coincides with it on all 4,000 pools.' candidate_selection.py lines 37-38: 'this rule is the best policy that clears the bar, and the probe checks that the module coincides with it.' docs/22 line 112 (Stage 3): a losing pair 'becomes a single row for its unshared allele in the same position ... or is removed when both of its alleles are claimed by pairs above it.'
blocking.evidence: The probe's direct+pays_gt is not the module's function, and it is not the Stage 3 policy the document describes. Two differences: (1) policy_probe.py _demote lines 106-107 drops a losing pair outright when its unshared single already sits above it, a branch the Review history row (line 189) says was 'removed with the rule change' and which Stage 3 does not describe; (2) _joint (lines 117-125) runs demotion to its own fixpoint before re-promoting, while resolve_rows (lines 303-312) re-promotes after every single demotion. Both differences are invisible in the probe's universe because it allows at most three alleles per gene (chr1 has 3, chr2 has 2, chr3 has 1), so the coincidence on 4,000 pools is an artifact of pool size. With four alleles in one gene they diverge: a 6-allele pool (below) gives module [(1:1000,1:2000),(1:3000,1:4000),2:2000,1:3000,3:1000,1:1000,1:2000,1:4000] and probe [(1:1000,1:2000),(1:3000,1:4000),1:3000,2:2000,1:4000,3:1000,1:1000,1:2000]; under truth (3:1000,2:2000) the module scores 25.0 and the probe 12.5. On a 10-allele, 4-gene universe at 5 to 9 rows (3,000 pools, seed 1, 66,211 comparisons) they differ on 519 pools; the probe's policy scores mean 37.810 against the module's 37.757 with both at 0 comparisons below the plain sort. Re-implementing the module's interleaving (one demotion, then re-promote) with the probe's demote body reproduces the module on all 3,000 pools, so the divergence is the loop structure plus the reintroduced drop branch. Consequence: the row labelled 'module' is the only row that measures the shipped code, the 'best policy that never hurts' label belongs to a different function that outscores the module once pools are larger than the probe can generate, and the document's own safeguard ('no two rows can be the same function unnoticed') was met by declaring two different functions the same. This is the same class of fault as B1 of the previous review, at the next size up.
